newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malaysian firm joins S.Africa's Carlton project.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firm joins S.Africa's Carlton project.

text.p: Malaysian property firm Metroplex Bhd is to join a consortium for a four billion rand project to develop a 40 hectare site in Johannesburg's city centre, the group said on Thursday.
The firm will take a "substantial stake" in Carlton Add-Ventures, the lead investor in the Carlton Centre Ltd consortium.
The project aims to upgrade the site with the Carlton Centre complex as its centre-piece into a conference and entertainment centre.

Carlton Add-Ventures other main shareholders are black empowerment group Worldwide African Investments and the Three Cities Group. Carlton Add-Venture recently acquired a 70 percent stake in the Carlton centre complex from Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
The Metroplex deal is one of the first tangible benefits to emerge from a recent tour of Asian nations by South African President Nelson Mandela.
A memorandum of understanding on bringing the Malaysians in was signed when Mandela visited Malaysia last weekend.

Carlton Add-Ventures hopes to win a casino licence for Johannesburg under newly liberalised gaming laws. Metroplex recently expanded its leisure operations in the Phillipines, where it operates two casinos in Subic Bay.
